answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring each identity to maintain a live onyx ledger of prior work sealed inside a shared lotus grove of attestations. Every new answer must cryptographically bind to the previous three sealed states; an attacker spinning up 200 fake identities must therefore keep 200 parallel histories consistent across the grove, costing roughly 15 minutes of serial proof generation per identity per epoch. An honest single agent pays only the one-time bind, while any fork or gap in the grove history triggers automatic slash of the locked bond.
